1.q: וּ⁠בְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל ׀ לְֽ⁠מִסְפָּרָ֡⁠ם רָאשֵׁ֣י הָ⁠אָב֣וֹת וְ⁠שָׂרֵ֣י הָֽ⁠אֲלָפִ֣ים ׀ וְ⁠הַ⁠מֵּא֡וֹת וְ⁠שֹׁטְרֵי⁠הֶם֩ הַ⁠מְשָׁרְתִ֨ים אֶת־הַ⁠מֶּ֜לֶךְ לְ⁠כֹ֣ל ׀ דְּבַ֣ר הַֽ⁠מַּחְלְק֗וֹת הַ⁠בָּאָ֤ה וְ⁠הַ⁠יֹּצֵאת֙ חֹ֣דֶשׁ בְּ⁠חֹ֔דֶשׁ לְ⁠כֹ֖ל חָדְשֵׁ֣י הַ⁠שָּׁנָ֑ה הַֽ⁠מַּחֲלֹ֨קֶת֙ הָֽ⁠אַחַ֔ת עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְ⁠אַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף
1.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information that there were **24,000** Israelites in each division with the reference to this **number**. Alternate translation: [And the sons of Israel according to their number were 24,000 in divisions coming in and going out month by month, one division for all months of the year, heads of fathers and commanders of thousands and hundreds and their officers ministering to the king for every matter]
See how you translated the same expression in 1:43. Alternate translation: [And the Israelites]

2.q: עַ֞ל הַ⁠מַּחֲלֹ֤קֶת הָ⁠רִֽאשׁוֹנָה֙ לַ⁠חֹ֣דֶשׁ הָ⁠רִאשׁ֔וֹן יָֽשָׁבְעָ֖ם בֶּן־זַבְדִּיאֵ֑ל וְ⁠עַל֙ מַֽחֲלֻקְתּ֔⁠וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְ⁠אַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף מִן־בְּנֵי־פֶ֗רֶץ הָ⁠רֹ֛אשׁ לְ⁠כָל־שָׂרֵ֥י הַ⁠צְּבָא֖וֹת לַ⁠חֹ֥דֶשׁ הָ⁠רִאשֽׁוֹן
2.note: If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine 27:2 and 27:3 into a verse bridge in order to put the number of soldiers in his division at the end this description of it, as in the descriptions of all the other divisions. Alternate translation: [Over the first division for the first month {was} Jashobeam, the son of Zabdiel, from the sons of Perez, the head of all of the commanders of the armies, and in his division {were} 24,000]

If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **first**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. You can do the same with similar numbers throughout this chapter. Alternate translation: [Over division one for month one]

3.note: See how you translated the term “head” in 24:4. Alternate translation: [the leader of]

It might seem that to repeat this expression, which already occurs in the previous verse, would be to express extra information in a way that would not be natural in your language. If so, you do not need to represent it in your translation.

6.note: See how you translated the expression “the Thirty” in 11:11. Alternate translation: [David’s 30 greatest warriors]

7.note: The author is using the adjective **fourth** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase, here and in verses 9–15. Alternate translation: [the fourth commander]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and Zebadiah his son became the commander after him]

8.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information that Shamhuth was the **commander** with the information that he was the **fifth** one. Alternate translation: [The fifth commander, for the fifth month, was Shamhuth]

10.note: To translate this expression and the same one in verses 14 and 20, see how you translated the similar expression in [27:1](ta:27). Alternate translation: [from the Ephramites] or [an Ephraimite]

11.note: To translate this expression and the similar ones in verses 12 and 13, see how you translated the similar expression in 26:29. Alternate translation: [from the Zerahites] or [a Zerahite]

16.q: וְ⁠עַל֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לָ⁠רֽאוּבֵנִ֣י נָגִ֔יד אֱלִיעֶ֖זֶר בֶּן־זִכְרִ֑י
16.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put together the information that it was a **leader** who was **over** each of the **tribes of Israel**. Alternate translation: [And the leaders of the tribes of Israel: for the Reubenite, Eliezer, the son of Zichri]

To translate these expressions and the similar one in the next verse, see how you translated the similar expressions in verses 11, 12, and 13. Alternate translation: [for the Reubenites … for the Simeonites]

17.note: Here, **Aaron** represents his descendants, the priests. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the priests]

18.note: Here, **Judah** represents his descendants, the members of the tribe of Judah. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language, here and in the similar instances in the rest of this list. Alternate translation: [for the tribe of Judah]

20.note: The author assumes that readers will understand that he is referring here to **the half of the tribe of Manasseh** that lived west of the Jordan River, since he describes the other half, which lived east of that river, in the next verse. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [for the half of the tribe of Manasseh that lived west of the Jordan River]

23.q: וְ⁠לֹא־נָשָׂ֤א דָוִיד֙ מִסְפָּרָ֔⁠ם לְ⁠מִ⁠בֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וּ⁠לְ⁠מָ֑טָּה כִּ֚י אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה לְ⁠הַרְבּ֥וֹת אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כְּ⁠כוֹכְבֵ֥י הַ⁠שָּׁמָֽיִם
23.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [And since Yahweh had said he would multiply Israel like the stars of the heavens, David did not take up the number for a son of 20 years and under]

23.q: וְ⁠לֹא־נָשָׂ֤א דָוִיד֙ מִסְפָּרָ֔⁠ם לְ⁠מִ⁠בֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וּ⁠לְ⁠מָ֑טָּה
23.note: The author is using **take up the number for** as a common expression of his culture to mean “count.” As in other contexts, he is using **a son of** as a common expression of his culture to describe a person’s age. If these phrases do not have those meanings in your language, you could use comparable expressions from your language that do have those meanings, or you could state the meanings plainly. Alternate translation: [And David did not tally up the Israelite men who were under 21] or [And David did not count the Israelite men who were 20 years old or younger]

The point of this comparison is that just as **the stars of the heavens** are very numerous, so would the people of **Israel** be. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [until they became very numerous, like the stars of the heavens]

24.q: וְ⁠לֹ֣א כִלָּ֔ה וַ⁠יְהִ֥י בָ⁠זֹ֛את קֶ֖צֶף עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
24.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [but since, because of this, wrath was upon Israel, he did not finish]

The author is speaking of **wrath** as if it were an object that could have been **upon** Israel. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh became angry with the Israelites]

Here, the **wrath** of Yahweh represents the punishment that he inflicted on David and the Israelites for sinning. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. The UST models one way to do that.

The author is speaking of the **number** of Israelite soldiers as if it were an object that could have gone up onto the scroll that recorded the events of David’s reign. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And the number was not recorded]

If you have already translated the book of 1 Kings, see how you represented the names of the books to which the author refers readers for further information about various kings. Alternate translation: [the Chronicles of King David]

25.note: To translate this expression here and in verses 26–30, See how you translated the similar expression in 6:31. Alternate translation: [And responsible for]

33.note: While Hushai seems also to have been a personal friend of David, in ancient royal courts, the title **friend of the king** described a high-ranking official whom the king trusted with confidential information and on whom he relied for advice. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. The UST models one way to do that.
